articles.title: Federal authorities step in: Clippers face criminal investigation following landmark sanctions in Kawhi Leonard case
articles.standfirst: Clippers face new federal pressure after NBA’s brutal Leonard punishment
articles.summary: Clippers face new federal pressure after NBA’s brutal Leonard punishment
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers were already preparing for a fight with the NBA over one of the harshest punishments in league history. A reported federal investigation has now made the situation considerably more serious.

According to The New York Times, federal prosecutors have opened a criminal inquiry into allegations surrounding the Clippers ’ financial arrangements connected to Kawhi Leonard . The probe is said to be in its early stages, with two subpoenas already issued.

That doesn't mean criminal charges are inevitable. Investigations can end without prosecution, and no wrongdoing has been established in court.

The development nevertheless places another layer of scrutiny on a franchise that was hit with sweeping penalties by the NBA only days earlier.

Clippers already fighting NBA findings

The league fined the Clippers $30 million, suspended owner Steve Ballmer for one year and stripped the organization of five future first-round picks following its investigation into alleged salary-cap circumvention.

The Clippers have rejected the conclusions and made clear they are considering every option available to challenge them.

“We vehemently reject the NBA’s findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence,” the team said in a statement.

The franchise also claimed that what the league communicated privately differed from what was ultimately announced publicly. At the center of the case are alleged off-court financial arrangements involving Leonard and companies connected in various ways to the Clippers .

Leonard hasn't admitted to violating league rules, but he issued a statement acknowledging problems involving people around him.

“Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am,” Leonard said. “I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused.”

Federal involvement changes the stakes

The NBA’s case concerns whether league rules were broken. A federal investigation operates under an entirely different standard. Prosecutors will be looking at whether any conduct potentially violated criminal law, which raises the stakes far beyond draft picks, suspensions and fines.

The Clippers are also reportedly weighing legal action against the NBA and could seek a restraining order in an attempt to block enforcement of the sanctions while any lawsuit proceeds.

That path would be difficult. Challenges to league discipline can face major legal hurdles, particularly when the governing rules provide broad authority to the commissioner and league office.

Still, Los Angeles has shown no sign of accepting the punishment quietly. The biggest uncertainty now is how far the federal inquiry goes.

At this stage, the investigation remains preliminary, and the existence of subpoenas doesn't establish guilt by the Clippers, Ballmer, Leonard or anyone else.

What is clear is that a controversy that began as an NBA compliance matter has now moved into a much more serious arena.

articles.title: Stephen Curry is amazed as he shoots hoops alongside a robot but never forgets what truly matters in life
articles.standfirst: The machine briefly stole the spotlight, but Curry turned an entertaining moment into a memorable experience
articles.summary: The machine briefly stole the spotlight, but Curry turned an entertaining moment into a memorable experience
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has spent his career making shots that sometimes seem impossible and, because of his extraordinary efficiency, almost mechanical. At Tsinghua High School in Beijing , however, he finally encountered a machine prepared to shoot beside him.

The robot entered the gym singing as Curry watched with a mixture of surprise and amusement. It then moved toward the court, raised the ball and began taking shots alongside the NBA’s all-time leader in three-pointers.

The students cheered as basketball and technology came together in a completely unexpected contest. It was not really Curry against the robot. Instead, Steph simply enjoyed the technological spectacle, studied its movements and allowed the machine to briefly become the star.

Steph Curry turns a futuristic moment into a deeply human lesson

The entertaining scene was only the beginning of a visit centered on something much more personal. Curry arrived at the school on September 10 to give more than 200 students what organizers described as their “first physical education class of the new school year.”

It was the first stop of his 2026 China tour following the announcement of a long-term partnership between Curry Brand and Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning. Instead of beginning the trip with a product presentation or exclusive event, Curry started inside a school gym, surrounded by young players who dream of improving.

His message addressed the doubts many young athletes carry before they ever step onto a major court.

“Height, talent and background are not limitations,” Curry told the students. “Passion and perseverance are the answer. Anything is possible.”

Those words sounded familiar because they reflected his own story. Curry entered the NBA surrounded by questions about his size, strength and ability to hold his own against bigger players. He responded by changing the way basketball is played and showing an entire generation that limitations do not always have the final word.

One of the most emotional moments involved Li Ruoxin, a girls’ basketball coach at the school. Ten years earlier, she had watched Curry from the stands as a student. This time, she stood beside him as a coach responsible for inspiring another generation.

Curry also honored the school’s basketball teachers during the visit, which coincided with Teachers’ Day in China . School officials later named him an honorary basketball advisor, giving the afternoon a meaning that extended far beyond the robot and its shots. The technology made the students laugh and cheer, but Curry gave them something more lasting.

The robot demonstrated what programming and innovation can accomplish. Curry reminded them what belief, repetition and years of perseverance can build in a human being.

The greatest shooter in NBA history shared the court with a machine designed to make baskets. The robot may have provided the surprise, but Curry made sure the young players left with the lesson.

articles.title: What does Jason Collins’ note say? Here’s what we know
articles.standfirst: Months before his death, the former player left written instructions about his personal belongings and the people he wanted to have in mind.
articles.summary: Months before his death, the former player left written instructions about his personal belongings and the people he wanted to have in mind.
articles.body:
A will can be enough to establish how someone’s assets should be distributed after their death. But in Jason Collins’ case, there was something more . Inside a safe deposit box, the former player left a note addressed to his executor with very specific instructions about some of his personal belongings, making clear not only what he wanted to happen to them, but also who should receive them.

The note was written during an especially difficult period. Collins signed his will in October 2025, months before his death and after he had been diagnosed with stage 4 glioblastoma . Now that his estate documents have been made public, the message offers a much more private look at some of his final wishes.

What does the note include?

The note contains specific instructions regarding the distribution of his jewelry, watches, silverware, clothing, cars and other personal belongings.

Although each of these items may seem like just another possession, together they represent things Collins acquired and used throughout his life. That is why, beyond whatever monetary value they may have had, he wanted to make clear what should happen to them and who should receive them after his death .

Who did he leave his belongings to?

The documents also reveal who was included in his final wishes.

His aunt Teri was named executor of the will . If she was unable to fulfill that responsibility, the alternate executors would be her husband, Brunson Green, and his twin brother, Jarron Collins.

His parents, brother, a cousin, husband and aunt are also listed among the beneficiaries.

In that sense, the note was not solely about his belongings. It was also part of a much broader decision about the people Collins wanted to include as he organized what he would leave behind .

His final wishes went beyond his family

But before getting into all of that, one question has inevitably begun to emerge:

How much money did Jason Collins leave behind?

The documents place the value of his personal property at more than $1.8 million . There may also be other assets held in private trusts, meaning that figure does not necessarily represent the full value of his estate.

articles.title: Lakers reportedly trying to trade Jarred Vanderbilt, Dalton Knecht before start of season
articles.standfirst: Los Angeles reportedly remains active on the trade market as the franchise looks to reshape its roster around Luka Doncic before the 2026-27 campaign begins
articles.summary: Los Angeles reportedly remains active on the trade market as the franchise looks to reshape its roster around Luka Doncic before the 2026-27 campaign begins
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers could still make another significant move before the 2026-27 NBA season gets underway, with Jarred Vanderbilt and Dalton Knecht reportedly emerging as the two players most likely to be moved.

According to Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer , the Lakers are still exploring trade possibilities involving both players as the franchise works toward finalizing its roster.

Los Angeles currently has 16 players on standard contracts and must get that number down to 15 before Opening Night.

That roster crunch gives the Lakers a practical reason to explore the trade market rather than simply releasing a player. Vanderbilt and Knecht have both previously appeared in trade rumors, and their situations make them logical names for the front office to investigate.

The possibility is particularly notable because both players traveled to Slovenia with the rest of the Lakers roster during Luka Doncic 's offseason minicamp.

Doncic organized the gathering in his home country as an opportunity for the revamped group to develop chemistry away from the pressure of the regular season. The trip featured basketball activities as well as social events and other team-building exercises.

Now, however, the Lakers may be prepared to make difficult personnel decisions as they attempt to build the strongest possible supporting cast around Doncic.

Why Vanderbilt and Knecht could be moved

Vanderbilt presents a complicated situation because of his contract. The defensive-minded forward has two years remaining on a deal worth $48 million, meaning a trade partner would have to take on significant salary.

His value on the court is also somewhat specialized. Vanderbilt can provide energy, rebounding and perimeter defense, but his offensive limitations, particularly as a shooter, have made it difficult for him to maintain a consistent role. Entering his fifth season with the Lakers, he has also faced periods of limited playing time under head coach JJ Redick.

Knecht's circumstances are different. The 25-year-old forward remains on his rookie contract after Los Angeles selected him 17th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft.

The Lakers have nevertheless struggled to establish him as a consistent part of their rotation. His situation became even more complicated after the franchise's bizarre trade involving the Charlotte Hornets in February 2025.

Los Angeles sent Knecht and other assets to Charlotte in a deal for center Mark Williams . However, Williams failed his physical, prompting the Lakers and Hornets to rescind the trade and send Knecht back to Los Angeles.

Since returning, Knecht has not developed into the reliable contributor the Lakers hoped he would become, and his reduced role has fueled speculation that the organization could eventually move on.

The timing of the latest reports is also significant because Los Angeles has spent much of the offseason attempting to address the roster around Doncic.

The Lakers added Walker Kessler to strengthen their interior presence and brought in several other players as they attempt to construct a more balanced team for their new era.

Their offseason plans also included an attempt to land Jonathan Kuminga , but the versatile wing ultimately chose the Minnesota Timberwolves on a two-year, $12.4 million contract.

Kuminga's decision leaves Los Angeles still searching for additional athleticism and defensive versatility on the wing. That could explain why Vanderbilt and Knecht are being considered as potential trade pieces rather than simply roster casualties.

For the Lakers, the objective is not necessarily to move either player for the sake of making a deal. The bigger priority is finding a player or package that better fits the roster surrounding Doncic and Austin Reaves.

With the season approaching, Los Angeles therefore has a relatively short window to decide whether Vanderbilt and Knecht remain part of the plan or become assets in another transaction.

The two players were recently teammates on a trip designed to build chemistry and establish a new identity. Yet with the Lakers still above the roster limit and reportedly seeking another wing upgrade, their futures in Los Angeles could now depend on what the front office can find on the trade market.

articles.title: Bronny James sees Lakers path clear after closest rival leaves for Luka Doncic's former team
articles.standfirst: Nick Smith Jr.'s move to Real Madrid removes one of Bronny's clearest competitors for backcourt minutes in Los Angeles.
articles.summary: Nick Smith Jr.'s move to Real Madrid removes one of Bronny's clearest competitors for backcourt minutes in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
Bronny James has been handed a potentially important opportunity with the Los Angeles Lakers after Nick Smith Jr. left the NBA to join Real Madrid , the club where Luka Doncic first established himself as a major European star.

Smith had been one of the guards competing directly with Bronny for minutes last season, but the Lakers declined his $2.49 million team option and allowed him to enter free agency.

His next move is now confirmed.

"Free agent guard Nick Smith Jr. has agreed to a one-year deal with Real Madrid, agents Lucas Newton and Calvin Andrews of Klutch Sports told @hoopshype," Michael Scotto reported.

"He averaged 7.6 points in 17.5 minutes during three NBA seasons with the Hornets and Lakers. He’ll be Real Madrid’s lead guard."

Bronny James gets more room in Lakers rotation

Smith's departure matters because he outperformed Bronny statistically during the previous campaign.

Smith averaged 6.2 points in 12.5 minutes across 30 games, shooting 43.5% from the field. Bronny appeared in 42 games but averaged 2.9 points in 8.9 minutes while shooting 40.9%.

The Lakers nevertheless made their priorities clear on June 29, fully guaranteeing Bronny's $2.3 million salary for the 2026 to 2027 season while declining Smith's option.

Bronny also showed there were no hard feelings about Smith's move, commenting on his former teammate's Instagram announcement: "Damn thats fire bro be great!!!"

JJ Redick has backed Bronny's development

Head coach JJ Redick has repeatedly spoken positively about Bronny's progress, particularly on the defensive end.

"I know there was a stretch recently where he didn’t shoot it well and of course, he had a nice shooting game against Utah," Redick said.

"He’s improved a ton defensively in terms of his body positioning, both on and off ball. We want him to continue to evolve as a disruptive defender as well."

That doesn't guarantee Bronny a major role, but one obvious competitor for minutes is now gone.

Smith has moved to the same European powerhouse where Doncic developed before joining the NBA, while Bronny remains in Los Angeles with another season to prove he deserves a bigger place in the Lakers ' rotation.

articles.title: LeBron James leads Team AlUla in Luanda in a billionaire battle on the water
articles.standfirst: The NBA star traveled to Angola to join Team AlUla at the Luanda Grand Prix, the fifth round of the E1 season, where his team starts third in the standings behind Tom Brady and Will Smith.
articles.summary: The NBA star traveled to Angola to join Team AlUla at the Luanda Grand Prix, the fifth round of the E1 season, where his team starts third in the standings behind Tom Brady and Will Smith.
articles.body:
L eBron James arrived in Luanda on Friday to accompany Team AlUla during the E1 Grand Prix. The NBA player thus made his first visit to Angola to support the team he owns during the fifth round of the championship.

This Saturday, September 12, LeBron landed on the Asian continent, pausing his offseason in the United States to make the trip across the Atlantic. He traveled with the aim of supporting his racing franchise, Team AlUla , which was competing in the UIM E1 Electric Boat World Championship in southern Africa.

LeBron James and a battle of stars on the water

Team AlUla arrives in Luanda in third place in the standings, with 75 points, after a difficult weekend in Monaco, where it earned just five points. The team is 35 points behind Will Smith's Westbrook Racing and 44 behind Tom Brady's Team Brady.

James has traveled to directly support his two main drivers, Spain’s Nerea Martí and Canada’s Rusty Wyatt , in a championship characterized by technical parity and mandatory gender equality in the lineups

The peculiarities of the vessels

The vessels used by the teams, known as RaceBirds, are identical for all participants and use hydrofoil technology that allows them to rise above the surface of the water when reaching top speeds of 93 kilometers per hour (50 knots).

articles.title: Steph Curry's limp during tour of China raises concerns about his knee ahead of training camp
articles.standfirst: The 38-year-old still believes he can play 70-plus games
articles.summary: The 38-year-old still believes he can play 70-plus games
articles.body:
S teph Curry ’s offseason was supposed to be about resetting after a frustrating injury-hit campaign. Instead, a few seconds of footage from China have reopened the biggest health question surrounding the Golden State Warriors .

Clips from Curry ’s Li-Ning “Wide Open Tour” appeared to show the 38-year-old moving cautiously and, at times, favoring a leg. He was also seen wearing a knee sleeve, enough to trigger concern among fans with training camp approaching.

There's been no official confirmation from Curry , the Warriors or Li-Ning of a new setback. Some later footage from the trip also showed him participating in basketball activities and moving more freely, so the videos alone cannot establish whether his knee has worsened.

The concern comes from what happened last season. Curry initially expected his right-knee problem to keep him out for only a short period.

“I thought I was going to be out a week,” he said. Instead, he missed 27 consecutive games and the 2026 All-Star Game before finally returning in April. Curry later explained that every attempt to progress his recovery seemed to trigger another reaction.

The issue may no longer be about recovery alone

Curry ’s knee trouble began in late January and was eventually diagnosed as patellofemoral pain syndrome, commonly known as runner’s knee.

Imaging reportedly showed no major structural damage, but the inflammation proved stubborn enough to keep him sidelined for nearly two months.

That history is why Warriors insider Monte Poole ’s recent reporting has drawn attention.

“There’s at least some lingering concern about the knee,” Poole said. “From what I’ve been told, it can be managed, but it has to be managed and that’s a new thing for Steph. People always say he is the most conditioned guy in the league, and now he has to manage a knee.”

Poole also reported that Curry and his training staff have developed ways to support the knee and work around the possibility that it may not feel completely normal.

That's a significant change for a player whose conditioning has long been one of his greatest strengths.

Golden State needs Curry available more than ever

There's also reason for optimism. Poole said Curry remains confident he can play “70-plus games,” suggesting the Warriors aren't preparing for another lengthy absence as things stand.

Golden State badly needs that confidence to prove justified. The Warriors went 9-18 during Curry ’s 27-game absence last season, and their margin for error entering 2026-27 is even smaller.

Jimmy Butler is recovering from a torn ACL, while Moses Moody is also expected to miss time as he rehabilitates a serious knee injury. That makes Curry ’s health more important than any individual viral clip.

The China footage shows how closely every movement will be watched after a knee problem that refused to disappear last season. And whether Curry can still perform at an elite level, and if Golden State can manage his body well enough to keep him on the floor.

articles.title: From the "witch hunt" to confessing the NBA's big scam: "I take responsibility"
articles.standfirst: Steve Ballmer, owner of the Clippers, confirmed that he had paid the fine
articles.summary: Steve Ballmer, owner of the Clippers, confirmed that he had paid the fine
articles.body:
Steve Ballmer , owner of the Los Angeles Clippers , accepts the sanctions imposed by the NBA on his franchise for the scam to circumvent the salary cap .'

" It has been a very difficult time for everyone associated with the Clippers, and I deeply regret the situation. I want to apologize to our fans, employees, and the other NBA team owners for the distraction and distress this matter has caused, and I take responsibility for it in my capacity as principal owner," the billionaire shared in a statement.

I want to apologize to our fans, employees, and the other NBA team owners

Steve Ballmer wanted to make it clear that "we are determined to leave this chapter behind. We have informed the NBA that we are complying with the sanctions imposed by the league, we have paid the fine, and we are moving forward".

We have informed the NBA that we are complying with the sanctions imposed by the league, we have paid the fine and we are moving forward

The Clippers' scam against the NBA with Kawhi Leonard becomes a criminal case

At the beginning of this month the NBA announced a series of harsh sanctions for the Clippers, including the loss of five future first-round Draft picks , a $30 million fine and a one-year suspension for Ballmer for violating the rules prohibiting circumvention of the salary cap, in a case related to Kawhi Leonard.

The investigation revealed a pattern of misconduct and multiple serious violations of the rules by the Clippers organization

The sanctions were imposed following an investigation of nearly a year into the franchise, which "revealed a pattern of misconduct and multiple serious violations of the rules by the Clippers organization, which had previously already violated the salary cap rules".

Initially, Ballmer and the Clippers flatly rejected the findings of the investigation; the team said it would challenge the league's decision "through every avenue available to us."

In a letter addressed to NBA commissioner Adam Silver, Ballmer's lawyer described the investigation as a "witch hunt" and the resulting sanctions as a "serious injustice" .

During the months leading up to the conclusion of the investigation, the Clippers remained firm in their position that they had not committed any wrongdoing and expected to be exonerated .

In the statement issued on Sunday, Ballmer noted that, although "disagreements over the report's conclusions persist," he did not want the matter to continue being a distraction.

articles.title: Clippers trade Kawhi Leonard to Raptors as federal investigation into salary cap circumvention escalates
articles.standfirst: Kawhi Leonard is heading back to Toronto after months of uncertainty surrounding the blockbuster deal
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard is heading back to Toronto after months of uncertainty surrounding the blockbuster deal
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard is finally heading back to the Toronto Raptors , bringing an end to a lengthy saga that was complicated by the NBA’s investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers.

The Clippers and Raptors have agreed to complete the blockbuster deal, with Toronto acquiring Leonard in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick , two unprotected first-round selections, a first-round pick swap and two second-round picks.

The agreement was initially reached in June but was put on hold while the league investigated potential salary-cap violations.

The NBA announced its findings on September 2, determining that the Clippers had engaged in a pattern of misconduct involving off-court income opportunities connected to Leonard .

The league said the organization helped facilitate endorsement arrangements with companies doing business with the team and failed to properly report certain activities.

The investigation had cast uncertainty over Leonard's future and delayed a trade that could now significantly reshape both franchises. With the league's ruling delivered, the Raptors and Clippers have been able to move forward with the long-discussed deal.

Toronto reunion finally becomes reality

The penalties imposed on Los Angeles were substantial. The Clippers lost five first-round picks covering the 2029 through 2033 drafts and were hit with a $30 million fine.

Owner Steve Ballmer received a one-year suspension, while several other senior Clippers executives were also suspended.

Leonard was fined $700,000 for his connection to the violations, but the NBA didn't suspend him or void his contract. The league also determined that his uncle, Dennis Robertson , played a role in facilitating the arrangements and prohibited him from conducting business with NBA teams and affiliates for five years.

Leonard's return carries enormous significance for the Raptors, as he spent the 2018-19 season in Toronto after arriving from San Antonio and immediately helped deliver the franchise's first NBA championship.

Leonard averaged 26.6 points per game during the regular season and raised that figure to 28.5 points during the Finals.

His memorable Game 7 buzzer-beater against the Philadelphia 76ers became one of the defining moments in franchise history before Toronto eventually defeated the Golden State Warriors to capture the championship.

Leonard's seven seasons with the Clippers have produced impressive individual numbers but considerably less postseason success.

He averaged a career-best 27.9 points per game last season, along with 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists, while shooting efficiently from the field and three-point range.

Despite his production, Los Angeles finished 42-40 and missed the playoffs, adding to the growing questions surrounding the team's direction.

Toronto, meanwhile, is coming off a 46-win campaign that ended with a first-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Raptors had returned to the postseason for the first time since 2022, giving the organization renewed optimism heading into the new season.

Now, Leonard's arrival could raise those expectations considerably. Toronto will look to combine his experience and scoring ability with a younger core led by Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett.

articles.title: Steve Kerr lays out a stark reality regarding LeBron James: "No one around the Bay wanted him to sign with the Warriors"
articles.standfirst: Warriors fans didn't want LeBron James after all, and Steve Kerr knows why
articles.summary: Warriors fans didn't want LeBron James after all, and Steve Kerr knows why
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors entered the offseason as one of the teams linked with LeBron James , creating the tantalizing possibility of the NBA legend joining forces with Stephen Curry.

That scenario ultimately never materialized, as James chose the Philadelphia 76ers after considering several potential destinations.

James ' arrival in the Bay Area never seemed particularly close to becoming reality for Warriors head coach Steve Kerr. ​ Speaking on the Tom Tolbert Show, Kerr acknowledged that Golden State's connection to James was driven more by speculation than concrete indications that a deal was imminent.

While many basketball fans would've been fascinated by the prospect of Curry and James sharing a Warriors uniform, some supporters apparently weren't disappointed when the opportunity disappeared.

The coach said people around the Bay have approached him and told him they were actually glad Golden State didn't acquire James .

"It's been really interesting, hearing fans around the Bay, people randomly will come up to me and say, 'I'm glad we didn't get LeBron,” said Kerr .

“I'm like, 'Really?' And they're like, 'Yeah. He's not supposed to be on our team, he's a rival.'"

That history is significant. James faced Golden State in four consecutive NBA Finals while playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2015 through 2018. The rivalry produced some of the most memorable moments of the era, including Cleveland's historic comeback from a 3-1 deficit in the 2016 Finals.

That history apparently made James feel like an opponent who some Warriors fans felt shouldn't suddenly become one of their own.

Kerr would've welcomed the opportunity

Kerr sees the situation differently from many of those fans. His experience coaching James with Team USA at the 2024 Paris Olympics gave him a firsthand look at what the superstar could bring to a team.

From a coaching perspective, Kerr said he'd have been eager to work with James again. He compared the unusual possibility to the idea of legendary rivals Magic Johnson and Larry Bird eventually becoming teammates.

“Just as a coach, and having coached him (LeBron) in the Olympics -- sign me up,” added Kerr .

Putting James alongside Stephen Curry would've been one of the league's most compelling combinations. Yet rivalries often carry an emotional weight that statistics and championship aspirations can't completely erase.

James ultimately chose Philadelphia, leaving Golden State without the blockbuster addition that had fueled plenty of offseason discussion. Kerr's remarks suggest the Warriors themselves never viewed the possibility as particularly close, despite the attention surrounding James and the franchise.

The Warriors also may not get another opportunity. James is 41 years old and is preparing for his 24th NBA season. Although he hasn't announced a firm retirement date, the latter stages of his career are clearly approaching.

The missed opportunity is less about disappointment and more about curiosity for Kerr , as having already coached James internationally, he would've welcomed the chance to see what the veteran superstar could accomplish alongside Curry .

Instead, Golden State will have to move forward without James .

The coach said people around the Bay have approached him and told him they were actually glad Golden State didn't acquire James .
"It's been really interesting, hearing fans around the Bay, people randomly will come up to me and say, 'I'm glad we didn't get LeBron,” said Kerr .
“I'm like, 'Really?' And they're like, 'Yeah. He's not supposed to be on our team, he's a rival.'"

That history is significant. James faced Golden State in four consecutive NBA Finals while playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2015 through 2018. The rivalry produced some of the most memorable moments of the era, including Cleveland's historic comeback from a 3-1 deficit in the 2016 Finals.
That history apparently made James feel like an opponent who some Warriors fans felt shouldn't suddenly become one of their own.
Kerr would've welcomed the opportunity

Kerr sees the situation differently from many of those fans. His experience coaching James with Team USA at the 2024 Paris Olympics gave him a firsthand look at what the superstar could bring to a team.

From a coaching perspective, Kerr said he'd have been eager to work with James again. He compared the unusual possibility to the idea of legendary rivals Magic Johnson and Larry Bird eventually becoming teammates.
“Just as a coach, and having coached him (LeBron) in the Olympics -- sign me up,” added Kerr .

Putting James alongside Stephen Curry would've been one of the league's most compelling combinations. Yet rivalries often carry an emotional weight that statistics and championship aspirations can't completely erase.

James ultimately chose Philadelphia, leaving Golden State without the blockbuster addition that had fueled plenty of offseason discussion. Kerr's remarks suggest the Warriors themselves never viewed the possibility as particularly close, despite the attention surrounding James and the franchise.

The Warriors also may not get another opportunity. James is 41 years old and is preparing for his 24th NBA season. Although he hasn't announced a firm retirement date, the latter stages of his career are clearly approaching.

The missed opportunity is less about disappointment and more about curiosity for Kerr , as having already coached James internationally, he would've welcomed the chance to see what the veteran superstar could accomplish alongside Curry .
Instead, Golden State will have to move forward without James .

articles.standfirst: Does the Golden State Warriors legend have a future in politics? The Arkansas Razorbacks head coach believes so.
articles.summary: Does the Golden State Warriors legend have a future in politics? The Arkansas Razorbacks head coach believes so.
articles.body:
After watching Donald Trump turn his entertainment and business career into a highly successful stint in the political world, calls for other celebrities to run for the presidency have never been higher. Even sports show talking head Stephen A. Smith has considered making a run.

Professional athletes are no strangers to those calls. The most charismatic of them have been told to give it a go if the opportunity arises. So far, it hasn't, but could Stephen Curry be the one to break the sports-political landscape? That's what John Calipari thinks could happen in the future - or at least that's what he wants to see .

John Calipari says Steph Curry is the one NBA player he wants to see get into politics

The current Arkansas Razorbacks head coach was recently stopped for a short interview by TMZ's Jacob Wasserman , who asked Calipari which NBA player he thinks should run for political office .

Steph Curry. But he would never do it. But he would be good because he cares about people. Really bright, energetic, has his beliefs and what he believes in, he’s going after. He’d be great... Whatever he wants, if he’s president, I want to be the ambassador to the Vatican. That’d be good.

Curry has spoken previously about the possibility of getting into politics. While explaining that he wants to help people by using his influence for good, he mentioned that " if politics is a way that you can create meaningful change or if there’s another way outside of politics ", then he'd be happy to try it out.

articles.title: NBA expansion to Las Vegas and Seattle could arrive as soon as the 2028-29 season
articles.standfirst: Just like the NFL, the NBA would expand to 32 teams, resulting in teams switching conferences
articles.summary: Just like the NFL, the NBA would expand to 32 teams, resulting in teams switching conferences
articles.body:
The NBA season is closer than you think, with the first regular season day starting in a little over a month on October 20 with three games, including the champion New York Knicks against the new Philadelphia 76ers with LeBron James .

But as the offseason continues, the annual NBA's Board of Governors meeting between commissioner Adam Silver and team owners is taking place this week with a couple of big announcements.

First, the union of the five largest American professional sports leagues ( NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS ) and their players' unions are urging state gambling regulators to combat escalating harassment and violent threats from sports bettors. And speaking solely of the NBA, momentum is accelerating rapidly regarding the addition of two expansion teams in Las Vegas and Seattle .

Billion-Dollar Bids for the NBA's 32-Team Expansion Plan

According to reports from ESPN , the financial scope of these prospective franchises has captured the entire sports world's attention, with Las Vegas ownership bids projected to exceed $10 billion , while a returning Seattle franchise is expected to hover around $7 billion .

To facilitate the transition, league operations indicate that a formal expansion draft would occur in the summer of 2028 , paving the way for both clubs to officially tip off as soon as the 2028-29 season .

Bringing two new squads into the fold will inevitably trigger major structural changes, most notably requiring conference realignment to balance out the Western Conference , where both geographically positioned markets naturally fit.

This historic milestone marks the league's first growth phase since the Charlotte Bobcats began play back during the 2004-05 season, finally ending a more than two-decade drought and expanding the association to 32 total teams .

articles.title: LeBron James conquers Angola: His first trip to Africa and the moment that went viral
articles.standfirst: LeBron James traveled to Angola for the first time to support his electric powerboat team
articles.summary: LeBron James traveled to Angola for the first time to support his electric powerboat team
articles.body:
LeBron James didn't go to Angola on vacation. He flew to Luanda to support his electric powerboat team, Team AlUla, at the UIM E1 World Championship . But what stole the internet was something much simpler: the 'King' dancing to African drums.

The trip marked his first visit to the African continent. LeBron arrived in Luanda on Saturday, September 12, 2026, just weeks before starting training camp with the Philadelphia 76ers . His official mission was clear: support his team, Team AlUla, at the fifth round of the electric powerboat world championship.

The event, the E1 Luanda GP 2026, took place in Luanda Bay and was the first time the championship raced in southern Africa, after its debut in Nigeria the year before. Team Brady took the win, while LeBron's team finished fourth in the overall standings. Will Smith, also a team owner, was there and shared the moment with LeBron in Luanda.

LeBron’s viral moment in Angola

But the moment that went viral happened off the water. At the Luanda waterfront, LeBron ran into a group of local drummers and dancers. Without hesitation, he joined the rhythm. The clip, shared by outlets like Afro Ballers, shows him smiling and following the beat of the drums, fully integrated with the people around him.

That same Sunday, LeBron also stopped to watch a 3x3 basketball showcase with young Angolan prospects on the Luanda boardwalk. There he met Angolan basketball legends like Miguel Lutonda, Nadir Manuel, Kikas Gomes, and Carlos Morais, figures from different generations of the national sport. Carlos Morais put it plainly: "It's an honor to have the 'King' in Angola, his first time in Africa. It's fantastic to have him here, trying our food, breathing our air."

Before the event, LeBron visited the National Museum of Slavery in Angola, a central place in the history of the transatlantic slave trade. "Obviously there's a lot of history here," he told reporters outside the museum. "A lot of history that's not just in this country, but also crosses over to America." According to local media, he got emotional during the guided tour.

On Sunday, LeBron and Will Smith were received at the Presidential Palace by President João Lourenço. The Angolan government used the event to project the country as a tourist and investment destination. "Our ambition is not simply to make Angola famous," Tourism Minister Márcio Daniel told the BBC. "It's to make Angola more desirable to visit, invest in, and do business with."

For the young people who saw LeBron in person, the moment was unforgettable. "One thing is seeing him on TV," Morais said, "another is seeing him in person. It means a lot to these kids." LeBron left Angola leaving behind an image that's hard to forget: a global superstar dancing, smiling, and connecting with people on his first visit to the African continent.

articles.title: Michael Jordan wore this jersey when he changed everything, now it could fetch $100 million
articles.standfirst: He wore this jersey when he changed everything
articles.summary: He wore this jersey when he changed everything
articles.body:
M ichael Jordan's Game 3 jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals, the only publicly known white Jordan jersey from that series, is heading to auction. The presale estimate is $10 million to $15 million. The owner thinks it could break every record in sports memorabilia.

There are game-worn jerseys, and then there's this. The white Chicago Bulls jersey Michael Jordan wore on June 7, 1998, during Game 3 of the NBA Finals against the Utah Jazz is officially up for auction through JOOPITER , the digital auction platform founded by Pharrell Williams. The sale, titled "Driven to Greatness," opens at 10:00 a.m. ET on September 15 and runs global bidding through September 29.

The jersey carries a presale estimate of $10 million to $15 million, but the current owner, sports investor and actor Rob Gough, believes it could go much higher. He told The Sporting News he thinks it could become the first sports jersey to sell for $100 million.

Why this specific jersey matters

Game 3 wasn't just another Finals game. It was the night the Bulls sent a message that echoed through the rest of the series. With the Finals tied 1-1 after two games in Utah, Chicago returned home and obliterated the Jazz 96-54 . That 42-point margin remains the largest in NBA Finals history. Utah's 54 points still stand as the fewest ever scored in a Finals game.

Jordan finished with 24 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals, and 1 block in just over 32 minutes of play. He didn't need a superhuman performance the Bulls' defense held Utah to 30% shooting and forced 26 turnovers. Karl Malone led the Jazz with 22 points, but no other Utah player scored more than 6.

The Bulls went on to win the series in six games, giving Jordan his sixth championship and sixth Finals MVP. It was the final title of the Bulls' dynasty and the last chapter of what became known as "The Last Dance".

The rarest Jordan jersey in existence

What makes this jersey exceptional isn't just the game, it's the scarcity. Game-worn Jordan Finals jerseys are among the most sought-after artifacts in sports collecting, but this one stands apart: it is the only publicly known white home jersey from the 1998 Finals to have ever surfaced.

Jordan's Game 1 jersey from that same series sold for $10.1 million in 2022, setting the record for a basketball jersey at public auction. That was a red road jersey. This white home version carries an additional layer of rarity.

The jersey features the coveted 1998 NBA Finals embroidered patch on the left chest. It comes with a MeiGray photomatching certificate and an official letter of provenance from Bill Thoma, the former Bulls equipment manager. Photomatching the process of matching a jersey to specific broadcast footage is the gold standard for authentication at this level.

The "Driven to Greatness" auction opens September 15 at 10:00 a.m. ET and runs through September 29. JOOPITER is hosting preview events in New York from September 15-20 and in Los Angeles from September 21-26.

For collectors, this is a rare window. A jersey with this combination of historical significance, verified authenticity, and extreme scarcity almost never reaches the open market. Whether it sells for $15 million or $100 million, one thing is certain: the jersey Jordan wore when he broke the Jazz will now carry a price tag that breaks records too.

articles.title: LeBron out, Wemby in? Stephen A. Smith crowns new NBA king
articles.standfirst: Has Victor Wembanyama finally surpassed LeBron James?
articles.summary: Has Victor Wembanyama finally surpassed LeBron James?
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama 's rise has brought a new question to the forefront of the NBA : is the league ready for a new face? Stephen A. Smith believes the San Antonio Spurs star has reached that point, even with LeBron James still active. Smith shared his assessment during an appearance on VT Gen Z , where he identified Wembanyama as the player currently positioned to represent the league. The declaration comes as the Frenchman's profile continues to grow.

“I think at this particular moment in time it's Victor Wembanyama,” Smith said. “But up until he arrived, I think you could still make an argument it was LeBron James. “I think LeBron James is still the preeminent face in the game based on his credentials, his resume, his lengthy history.” The sports personality was careful to distinguish Wembanyama 's growing influence from James ' enduring legacy. Smith acknowledged that the ex- Los Angeles Lakers star's accomplishments and longevity continue to make him a central figure in basketball. Wembanyama 's appeal extends beyond his extraordinary height. At 7-foot-4, the Frenchman combines rim protection with mobility and perimeter shooting, making him a distinctive representative of the modern NBA . His emergence has also been accompanied by individual recognition and team success. Coming off a Defensive Player of the Year campaign, Wembanyama has continued to establish himself as one of basketball's most prominent young stars. James ' career has spanned more than two decades, beginning with his arrival in the NBA in 2003. His journey from a high school phenomenon in Akron, Ohio, to one of basketball's defining figures has made him a lasting presence. But Smith 's comments reflect that changing landscape, as although the veteran James still commands attention and respect, a new generation inevitably builds its own identity. “But Wembanyama has definitely arrived, and the Wemby era is definitely here even though he just lost in the Finals,” Smith concluded of Wembanyama , who, represents a different kind of superstar: a young international talent.

Why LeBron chose the 76ers according to Dwyane Wade

While Smith discussed the NBA 's changing face, Dwyane Wade recently offered his perspective on James ' basketball future, arguing the Philadelphia 76ers could provide a strategic opportunity at this stage of his career. Wade explained why he believed the 76ers offered a strong path toward another championship opportunity as he approaches the end of his career. “From a basketball standpoint,” Wade said to the Conversations with Cam Podcast. “I thought it is a very strategic move at this point in his career. It definitely gives him the best chance... “I feel like it gives him the best chance in the East to be able to get back to compete for a championship.” His comments show the immense and continued interest in James ' next chapter, even at the age of and as Wembanyama 's rise begins to catch more headlines.

articles.summary: LeBron James, who agreed to the largest salary reduction in NBA history, will make more money thanks to his partnership with Polymarket than playing for the Sixers
articles.body:
L eBron James the Sixers ' star signing this summer, agreed to the largest pay cut in NBA history by signing a 2-year, $8 millioin contract with Philadelphia .

The 41-year-old forward has gone from earning 52.3 million in his final season with the Lakers to the 3.8 he accepted from the Sixers for the current campaign.

LeBron James, who l oses 48.75 million from one season to the next in pursuit of the goal of competing for the championship in the City of Brotherly Love, has taken an stunning 92% reduction compared to his previous salary .

Controversial LeBron James deal with a betting company: he will earn triple what he makes with the Sixers

Over his more than two decades of career in the NBA, he has earned 583.9 million in contracts , but his net worth is much greater thanks to his investments and advertising income (he has a lucrative lifetime contract with Nike that brings him in 40 million annually).

Other companies that are betting heavily on LeBron include Polymarket (in September it signed him to a 15-million-a-year contract as an ambassador for the betting company) , PepsiCo, Richard Mille, and Mattel (he became the first professional athlete to have his own Ken doll), AT&T, Beats by Dre, GMC, Rimowa, and Walmart.

To expand and consolidate his fortune, LeBron James has managed to replace cash payments with equity stakes in companies he collaborates with, such as Apple and Blaze Pizza.

According to Forbes, "King" James has an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion .

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal changes his father’s life forever to repay everything he did for him
articles.standfirst: Shaquille O’Neal changed his father’s life forever after he raised him on an Army salary
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal changed his father’s life forever after he raised him on an Army salary
articles.body:
Long before Shaquille O’Neal became an NBA superstar, Phillip Harrison was simply Dad . The Army sergeant was technically Shaq’s stepfather, but he raised him from early childhood, provided discipline when money was tight and moved the family wherever his military career took them. Decades later, when Shaq finally started making serious money, one of his first priorities was making sure Harrison would never have to worry about his own paycheck again.

From an Army salary to a life-changing paycheck

After entering the NBA, O’Neal created Shaq, Inc. and gave his parents actual jobs running his fan club, complete with a workspace and responsibilities. According to Shaq's own account, Harrison initially resisted because he wanted to continue working on an Army base. Then Shaq asked him a simple question: how much was he earning? The answer was about $60,000 a year.

Shaq's response changed the conversation immediately. He told Harrison he would now make $500,000 a year working for him. O'Neal recalled that his father started crying. He then turned to his mother, Lucille, and put her on an even larger salary: $750,000 a year.

Shaq never forgot who was there before the millions

The gesture carried considerably more meaning than simply giving his parents money. Harrison had raised Shaq while serving in the Army, moving the family through places including New Jersey, Georgia and Germany. O'Neal has repeatedly credited his father's strict upbringing with helping turn a troublesome kid into the disciplined player who eventually became one of basketball's biggest stars. Harrison died in 2013.

And Shaq's financial support wasn't limited to salaries. By the mid-1990s, reports were already documenting that he had bought his mother a house and regularly offered to buy her new cars. For a player who would ultimately earn roughly $292 million in NBA salary alone , taking care of the people who supported him before the fame became part of how he used that success.

There was also a smart business move behind the gift

Shaq wasn't simply handing his parents enormous checks. Because they performed legitimate work for his company, their compensation could be treated as a business expense subject to applicable tax rules. The IRS permits businesses to employ family members, although wages still need to correspond to genuine work and the appropriate payroll and tax requirements apply.

For Shaq, however, the emotional part of the story is simpler. The man who raised him on an Army salary eventually worked for the son he helped raise for $500,000 a year. Harrison had spent Shaq's childhood trying to change the direction of his son's life. Once Shaq had the means, he returned the favor.

articles.title: Steph Curry thwarts LeBron James' strategy: The only NBA trend the Warriors star refuses to follow
articles.standfirst: Curry does not intend to walk out on Golden State.
articles.summary: Curry does not intend to walk out on Golden State.
articles.body:
LeBron James changed teams again this summer, but Stephen Curry has made it clear that his own NBA journey is heading in a very different direction. James ended his eight-year run with the Los Angeles Lakers after deciding to join the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, eight-million-dollar deal, giving the four-time champion a fresh title chase.

Curry , meanwhile, is entering the final year of his Golden State Warriors contract, creating speculation about whether James ' decision could influence his own plans. But the iconic basketballer, famed for his ability to shoot from range, was emphatic. “Not at all,” Curry said to CNBC. “I’ve always stated that I want to be a lifer with Golden State, what we’ve built there, the fact that I get to run it back this year with Draymond [Green] and Coach Kerr. “So all the contract stuff, this NBA thing from year to year is so crazy. Things change really fast, but I do know my interest and mission to stay in Golden State and be competitive is there, and the contract stuff will take care of itself.” The Warriors have also made their intentions clear as general manager Mike Dunleavy has said Golden State plans to offer Curry a two-year, $136.7 million extension, while acknowledging the final decision remains with the franchise icon. “I’m pretty confident Steph will finish his career here,” Dunleavy said. “But ultimately, it’s his call, his decision. We wouldn’t love it, but he’s earned the right to go where he wants.” So, whilst James has embraced another franchise and another challenge late in his career, Curry has repeatedly indicated that he wants his legacy to remain tied to Golden State . The Warriors ' next contract decision will determine when that commitment becomes official, but Curry has already drawn a clear line between his future and James ' latest career move.

Can the Philadelphia 76ers win the NBA Finals with LeBron?

Philadelphia 's decision to add James came after an aggressive offseason that also brought Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics . Paul George and a healthy dose of draft compensation is heading in the opposite direction to Massachusetts in the blockbuster trade. Brown joins James , Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey , giving the 76ers a dramatically reshaped core after the team finished 45-37 in the 2025/26 NBA season. The 76ers found themselves eliminated in the first round of the playoffs but that could be different this time around as James arrives after telling fans that winning remains central to his decision. The legendary player vowed his goal is to take the 76ers to the NBA Finals – but he major question now centers on whether that star power can actually do it. Philadelphia has assembled significant talent, but Embiid 's availability remains an important variable after he appeared in only 39% of the team's games over the previous three seasons. Whilst LeBron is supremely talented, he not getting any younger in his age 42 season so could the miles on the clock be too much for the 76ers veterans?

articles.title: Michael Sweetney cause of death: the college star whom depression kept from shining in the NBA dies at 43
articles.standfirst: Former Knicks and Bulls player
articles.summary: Former Knicks and Bulls player
articles.body:
"M ichael Sweetney, former Knicks and Bulls player, has died this Thursday at the age of 43 . It was his own wife, India, who announced the news through a post on social media. The causes of death of the 2.03-meter power forward are unknown.

Sweetney was a star at Georgetown University , where in his final season, 2002-03, he posted monstrous averages of 22.8 points, 10.4 rebounds, 3.2 blocks, 1.9 assists and 1.5 steals per game . That put him among the candidates for prestigious honors such as the Naismith College Player of the Year award and helped him rise in draft projections.

Finally, he was selected by the Knicks with the ninth pick in 2003 . However, upon arriving in the NBA, he was never able to live up to expectations due to mental health problems. His father died just before the start of his rookie season, and that sent him into a deep depression . Added to the lack of playing time, Sweetney ended up suffering from eating disorders that led to excessive overweight .

Severe overweight problems

At just 2.03 meters tall, Sweetney came to weigh around 150 kilos when he played in the NBA. In later stages, several dozen more . Even so, he played two seasons in New York before being traded to the Bulls in a deal that included Eddy Curry, Tim Thomas and Antonio Davis. Between his two stints, he played 233 games in the American league, averaging 6.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in 15.5 minutes on the court .

When the doors of the NBA closed, the power forward became a globetrotter. He played for teams in China, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, and Uruguay before retiring in 2017.

After leaving basketball, drawing on his own experience, Sweetney worked to expose mental illnesses and spoke publicly about what he had suffered at the start of his NBA career, when everything he had shown promise for as a college player came to little because of the depression he suffered .

articles.title: Michael Sweetney's wife in emotional tribute after former Knicks star dies at 43
articles.standfirst: First-round pick was remembered for devotion to family and his openness about mental health
articles.summary: First-round pick was remembered for devotion to family and his openness about mental health
articles.body:
M ichael Sweetney ’s death at 43 has prompted tributes across the basketball world, but the most personal words came from the woman who knew him long before Madison Square Garden, the NBA Draft or the expectations that followed him into professional basketball.

His wife, India Sweetney , announced his death Thursday, Sept. 17, in an emotional message that focused on the husband, father and friend behind the former New York Knicks forward.

“With the heaviest hearts, we are deeply saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Michael,” she wrote. “To know @mikesweetney was to love him.”

India said Sweetney ’s children “were the light of his life” and described him as her best friend of 30 years and husband of nearly two decades.

“He was the best son, brother, family member, friend, father and husband ANYONE could ask for,” she wrote.

Sweetney once carried huge expectations

Long before his NBA career, Sweetney built his reputation at Georgetown, where he became one of the most productive big men in college basketball.

He averaged 18.2 points and 9.2 rebounds across three seasons with the Hoyas, then raised his production to 22.8 points and 10.4 rebounds per game as a junior.

That performance made him a highly regarded prospect, and the Knicks selected him ninth overall in the 2003 NBA Draft.

Sweetney spent two seasons in New York before being traded to the Chicago Bulls in 2005 as part of the deal that sent Eddy Curry and Antonio Davis to the Knicks .

He later played two seasons in Chicago and finished his NBA career with averages of 6.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in 233 games.

His playing career continued overseas before he eventually moved into coaching, including a role as an assistant at Yeshiva University beginning in 2019.

Impact went well beyond NBA career

Sweetney ’s post-playing years added another dimension to his legacy.

He spoke candidly about depression and the grief he experienced after his father’s death, using his own struggles to encourage more open conversations about mental health in sports.

That willingness to speak publicly about difficult periods became an important part of how he was viewed after basketball. The Knicks also paid tribute to their former first-round pick following news of his death.

“Michael was an incredible person who will be missed by many,” the team said.

India Sweetney ’s message, though, placed his legacy in more intimate terms.

The former Knicks forward may be remembered by fans as a lottery pick from one of the NBA’s most famous draft classes, and by Georgetown supporters as an imposing frontcourt presence.

Inside his family, his identity was simpler and more important. He was the person who, as his wife put it, spent every day trying to give his children the best life possible.

articles.title: Shaquille O'Neal, former NBA player and entrepreneur: "Never worry about the problem. Always worry about the solution"
articles.standfirst: Shaq’s solution-first mindset offers a useful lesson far beyond basketball
articles.summary: Shaq’s solution-first mindset offers a useful lesson far beyond basketball
articles.body:
Shaquille O’Neal spent much of his basketball career overpowering defenders, but one of his most useful ideas has nothing to do with strength.

“Never worry about the problem. Always worry about the solution,” O’Neal said.

The quote sounds simple, but it reflects a mindset that defined much of his career. O’Neal wasn't arguing that problems should be ignored. His point was that once a setback has been identified, dwelling on it does little good unless that attention leads to action.

That distinction matters in sports, business and ordinary life. A mistake can be analyzed. A loss can be understood. A difficult situation can be acknowledged. But eventually, the focus has to shift to what comes next.

A career built on responding to pressure

O’Neal entered the NBA in 1992 after starring at LSU and quickly became one of the league’s most dominant centers.

He won four NBA championships, earned the league MVP award in 2000 and built a Hall of Fame career before retiring in 2011. Along the way, he also dealt with criticism, pressure and the expectations that came with being one of basketball’s biggest stars.

Criticism can become a problem if it consumes someone. It can also become information, fuel or motivation, depending on how it is handled. O’Neal has spoken about leadership in similar terms.

Real lesson is about where energy goes

The practical value of O’Neal ’s quote is in deciding what deserves attention.

People cannot always control whether a problem appears. They can often control whether they spend all of their energy reliving it or begin working toward a response.

That could mean adjusting after a mistake at work, changing an approach after a failed project or simply deciding not to let one difficult moment define everything that follows.

O’Neal ’s own life after basketball reflects that adaptability. He moved into broadcasting, business and entrepreneurship, building a second career rather than allowing retirement from the NBA to become an ending.

“I was taught and raised to never give up, always persevere and no excuses,” he once said.

The problem may be unavoidable. The response is where the opportunity begins.

articles.title: Knicks’ greed sparks outrage and forces team to suspend ticket sales
articles.standfirst: The cheapest seat for the season opener surpassed $1,000
articles.summary: The cheapest seat for the season opener surpassed $1,000
articles.body:
T he celebration of the New York Knicks’ first championship in 53 years quickly turned into outrage. Tickets for their October 20 season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers appeared at astonishing prices: the cheapest seat reached $1,251 and climbed as high as $1,408 during a presale.

The backlash forced Madison Square Garden Sports to temporarily suspend individual ticket sales. The organization acknowledged that an internal error had caused the increase and insisted it never intended to overcharge its fans.

The Knicks will return to last season’s prices and apply an average increase of 12%, the same hike established for season tickets. Anyone who already purchased tickets at the incorrect prices will receive a refund for the difference.

“We are pausing Knicks individual ticket sales due to a mistake in our pricing,” an MSG spokesperson said. “Our intention was never to overcharge our loyal fans, and we thank everyone for their support of the Knicks and their patience as we get this right.”

The error had pushed the average price for opening night to approximately $2,500. Demand is particularly high because the Knicks will raise their championship banner against a revamped 76ers team led by Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey alongside new stars LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

The organization will resume sales once the corrected prices become available. Although the mistake will be fixed, the 12% increase confirms that watching the champions at Madison Square Garden will remain considerably more expensive this season.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo makes a nod to Jimmy Butler with iconic new look in Miami
articles.standfirst: The NBA superstar is settling in very nicely in South Florida, and he wants everyone to know about it.
articles.summary: The NBA superstar is settling in very nicely in South Florida, and he wants everyone to know about it.
articles.body:
Some true stars switched NBA teams this past offseason. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown both joined the Philadelphia 76ers . LaMelo Ball went to the Minnesota Timberwolves . Kawhi Leonard returned to the Toronto Raptors .

But the biggest move may well have been Giannis Antetokounmpo leaving the Milwaukee Bucks after 13 seasons. Welcoming him with open arms were the Miami Heat , who are hoping Giannis is the " whale " the franchise hasn't been able to land since they got Jimmy Butler back in 2019.

Giannis Antetokounmpo is embracing the Miami lifestyle: Bright colors and cafecito

Many have wondered if it will take Antetokounmpo some time to get acclimated to South Florida after so much time up north. So far, so good on that front . In case anyone was wondering about that, Giannis published a photo on social media that's as Miami as it gets: sporting Miami Vice colors and sipping an espresso (probably a Cuban cafecito) .

The coffee stood out in particular. Many might remember that Butler started up his own coffee business while he was with the Heat . Called " BigFace ", it all began during the Heat's run to the NBA Championship during the 2020 COVID "bubble" season . Butler's love of coffee led to him making cups of it for players in the bubble, and charging them, of course.

Butler then launched the coffee and lifestyle brand officially the year after. Perhaps Giannis is thinking of doing something similar. Or he's just enjoying the cafecitos he missed out on before he was in Miami.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal, recently appointed as an FBI special agent, calls for Charles Barkley’s “arrest” on Inside the NBA
articles.standfirst: Shaq uses FBI graduation speech to send Barkley a hilarious warning
articles.summary: Shaq uses FBI graduation speech to send Barkley a hilarious warning
articles.body:
Shaquille O’Neal has added another unexpected title to his remarkable résumé, but he couldn’t help but use the occasion to take another playful shot at Charles Barkley.

The four-time NBA champion was named an honorary FBI Special Agent by FBI Director Kash Patel during the graduation ceremony for the FBI National Academy’s 299th session in Quantico, Virginia, on Thursday, September 17. The session included 265 law enforcement officials from across the country.

O’Neal addressed the graduating class and offered encouragement before turning his attention to his longtime television colleague.

After discussing the different paths the graduates could take, the Hall of Famer ended his remarks with a characteristically Shaq-style punchline.

“Some of you will go back to your regular jobs, some of you will go to specialized training,” O’Neal told the graduating class.

“Some of you will go do what I do, be undercover. Well, I was undercover… But I just wanna say I appreciate you guys so much. Congratulations. I am not here for this; I am here for you. … And if you see Charles Barkley, arrest him.”

The comment was the latest chapter in the light-hearted rivalry between two former NBA opponents who’ve since become close friends and television partners. Their relationship has been built on years of teasing, particularly during their time together on Inside the NBA.

Shaq’s law enforcement connection goes back years

While the FBI honor is ceremonial, O’Neal’s connection to law enforcement isn’t new. The former Los Angeles Lakers and Miami Heat star has pursued police training and served in reserve law enforcement roles during and after his NBA career, including positions connected to Los Angeles, Miami Beach and Doral, Florida.

His interest in policing has also been influenced by his family. O’Neal has previously spoken about how his father taught him to respect police officers and the work they perform, helping shape his longstanding interest in law enforcement.

The honorary FBI designation adds another chapter to that unusual part of his post-playing career. However, the title doesn't mean O’Neal has become a sworn FBI investigator or gained the authority associated with an actual special agent.

The National Academy is also separate from the FBI’s basic training program for newly hired special agents, as it’s a professional development program for experienced law enforcement personnel.

O’Neal’s new honor also comes after years of publicly supporting law enforcement. Patel described him as one of the FBI’s prominent supporters when announcing the recognition.

As for Barkley and O’Neal , heir rivalry dates back to the 1990s, when they faced each other on the court. Decades later, that competitive relationship has evolved into a television friendship, with O’Neal and Barkley continuing to trade jokes whenever the opportunity arises.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg are giving Dallas hope: ‘Like watching Picasso paint’
articles.standfirst: The preseason workouts could prove invaluable when it matters most
articles.summary: The preseason workouts could prove invaluable when it matters most
articles.body:
T he Dallas Mavericks know talent alone will not carry them through an 82-game season. With expectations rising and several key pieces preparing for larger roles, the franchise appears focused on building something just as important as skill: chemistry. That process has already begun thanks to Kyrie Irving.

The veteran guard recently hosted a series of offseason workouts in Los Angeles , inviting Mavericks teammates to join him ahead of training camp. While the sessions allowed players to sharpen their games before the regular season, they also served a larger purpose—strengthening relationships, establishing trust, and laying the foundation for what Dallas hopes will be a deep postseason run.

For a team built around emerging superstar Cooper Flagg and a returning Irving, those workouts could prove invaluable. Flagg , who captured Rookie of the Year honors after averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 4.5 assists across 70 games last season, was among the players who benefited from spending time on the court with the eight-time All-Star.

“Kyrie is obviously one of the greats,” Flagg told reporters. “So just to be able to share the floor with him, learn from him on the fly, and compete with him, it’s going to be a lot of fun.”

One of the NBA’s most respected veterans

The comments reveal more than simple admiration. They underscore the importance of Irving’s presence within a Mavericks roster that is blending youth, experience, and championship aspirations. For Flagg, the challenge entering his second NBA season is significantly different from the one he faced as a rookie. Opponents now have a full season of film on him. Defenses will be designed specifically to limit his strengths.

Expectations are higher. Every performance will be scrutinized. That is where Irving’s influence could become especially important. Few guards in league history possess the combination of creativity, ball-handling skill, and offensive imagination that Irving brings to the floor.

Even after spending 19 months recovering from a torn ACL , he remains one of the NBA’s most respected veterans and a player capable of elevating teammates around him. The chemistry-building sessions in Los Angeles offered Dallas an early opportunity to explore what a Flagg-Irving partnership might look like before the games begin to count.

Head coach Dusty May came away impressed by what he witnessed.

“I felt like I was watching Picasso paint a picture,” May said of the interactions between the two stars. That kind of praise reflects the potential Dallas sees in the pairing. Flagg is one of the league’s brightest young talents, while Irving provides the experience of a former champion who has performed on basketball’s biggest stages. Together, they could form one of the NBA’s most intriguing duos.

The Mavericks appear to be taking a long-term view

Still, the Mavericks understand there are legitimate questions that will not be answered until the season starts. Irving is no longer the 31-year-old guard who could rely almost entirely on athletic explosiveness. He enters the campaign at 34 years old and is returning from a lengthy ACL rehabilitation process . While modern sports medicine has extended careers and improved recovery outcomes, there remains uncertainty whenever a veteran player returns from a major injury.

Dallas is betting that Irving’s recovery will allow him to remain a high-level contributor throughout the season. His agent, Shetellia Riley Irving, recently emphasized that the focus has been on ensuring he is fully healthy and positioned to compete for another championship.

The Mavericks appear to be taking the same long-term view. Rather than simply preparing for opening night, they are working to build the connections that could matter most in April, May, and June. That is why the Los Angeles workouts carry significance beyond conditioning drills and pickup games.

Teams often talk about culture and chemistry, but those qualities are developed through shared experiences long before the regular season begins. Players learn each other's tendencies, communicate more naturally, and build confidence in one another.

articles.title: Stephen Curry breaks silence on secret attempt to recruit LeBron James
articles.standfirst: Stephen Curry finally revealed his role in trying to recruit LeBron James.
articles.summary: Stephen Curry finally revealed his role in trying to recruit LeBron James.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors had a clear target in free agency: LeBron James . The organization did everything it could to convince the four-time NBA champion to join forces with Stephen Curry , but the effort ultimately fell short. The veteran superstar instead signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

For weeks, rumors swirled about Curry’s role in the recruitment process. After all, the two have been the defining faces of the NBA for the better part of a decade. Despite the mutual respect between them, LeBron never ranked Golden State among his top options, prioritizing offers from Eastern Conference teams instead.

Now, for the first time since free agency concluded, Curry has broken his silence on the attempt to land James — and made it clear he never would have passed up the chance to try.

“If anybody didn’t [try to recruit him], I think they’d be a fool. It was a good time for the NBA — obviously with a guy of his stature, his notoriety, to be in that position where he got to choose where he wanted to go.”

With those words, the two-time MVP confirmed he played an active role in the recruitment. At the same time, he made clear that he fully respected James’s decision as the league’s all-time leading scorer.

The mission was always an uphill battle. With Jimmy Butler sidelined by injury, Curry is currently the only All-Star caliber player on the Warriors’ roster. Beyond him, Draymond Green — one of LeBron’s closest friends in the league — was the only other figure with enough influence to try to sway him.

In the end, neither Curry nor Green could convince James that Golden State’s current roster had what it took to contend for another championship.

The move LeBron was waiting for never came

Throughout free agency, reports indicated that James was open to considering either the Warriors or the Cleveland Cavaliers — but with one major condition: that one of the teams make a significant roster upgrade before he arrived.

Golden State chose to keep its core intact and attempted to recruit James without making a blockbuster trade.

One of the most frequently mentioned names was Anthony Davis , who would have formed a star trio alongside Curry and LeBron while reuniting James with his former Los Angeles Lakers teammate. The Washington Wizards, however, showed no interest in trading Davis before he even debuted with the franchise, effectively shutting the door on that possibility.

Meanwhile, the Philadelphia 76ers stunned the league by acquiring Jaylen Brown in exchange for Paul George — a move that ultimately proved decisive in landing LeBron.

Brown arrives after the best season of his career and represented exactly the kind of high-impact addition James was looking for on a true title contender.
