articles.title: A young man paid three dollars for a jacket from a second-hand store: they discovered it was worn by Wilt Chamberlain in the 1972 NBA Finals and sold it for 90,000
articles.standfirst: The teenager's name is Quinn Brown
articles.summary: The teenager's name is Quinn Brown
articles.body:
19-year-old Quinn Brown , a vintage clothing reseller from Portland, Oregon, bought a Los Angeles Lakers warm-up jacket for just $3.07 at a Goodwill outlet store in Hillsboro. What he did not know at the time was that the garment was hiding a big secret that would allow him to receive a major financial windfall.

After meticulous verification, the prestigious auction house Sotheby's confirmed through ‘photo-matching’ (matching seams and photographic details) that it was the original jacket worn by the legend Wilt Chamberlain during the 1972 NBA Finals.

The market for Wilt Chamberlain historical and collectible items moves millions

Quinn noticed that another buyer had dismissed it and returned it to the used clothing bins, but upon seeing its gigantic size (suitable for someone 2.16 meters tall) and the surname “Chamberlain” embroidered on it, he decided to buy it. Experts forensically compared the stitching of the yellow and purple jacket with old photographs from the 1972 Finals games against the New York Knicks, where Chamberlain was named MVP.

Finally, the iconic garment was officially auctioned by Sotheby's for a final price of $89,600 . It should be noted that the market for Wilt Chamberlain's historical and collectible items moves millions, since we are talking about one of the most dominant players in NBA history .

A jersey also from the 1972 Finals (Lakers) sold for $4,900,000 and is the most expensive Chamberlain item in history. However, in addition to it and this jacket, a 1959-60 rookie uniform (Warriors) sold for $1,792,000 and a leather disco suit (1970s) sold for $20,000 .

articles.title: Emotional message from Doncic to his daughters after leaving them to go with the Lakers
articles.standfirst: Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!
articles.summary: Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!
articles.body:
Luka Doncic returns to the United States after having spent much of the postseason in Slovenia.

To join the Los Angeles Lakers preseason, the former Real Madrid player has had to leave his two daughters (Gabriela (2023) and Olivia (2025) in his homeland in the care of his ex Anamarie Goltes .

G+O, it doesn't matter what part of the world Dad is in. Not a day goes by without you being in my heart

Doncic was publicly seen to be affected by having to separate from his two daughters , something he expressed on Sunday through a moving Instagram post that included several family photos.

"G+O, no matter what part of the world Dad is in. Not a day goes by without you being in my heart. Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!" the Lakers star shared with his more than 10.8 million followers on Instagram.

Tough legal battle for Luka Doncic with his ex Anamaria Goltes over custody of their daughters

Luka Doncic has lived through a turbulent year with regard to his family life, starring in a tough legal battle with Anamaria Goltes over custody of their daughters .

"I love my daughters more than anything in the world, and I have done everything possible for them to be with me in the United States, but it has not been possible. Everything I do is for their happiness, and I will always fight to be with them and give them the best life possible," Doncic said in March 2026.

In August, Anamarie Goltes, who maintains her residence in Slovenia, filed a request to withdraw her child support petition for her daughters against Luka Doncic.

articles.title: 'Michael Jordan: "I have failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed"'
articles.standfirst: In a historic 1997 Nike commercial, the Chicago Bulls legend chose to talk about his mistakes instead of his titles.
articles.summary: In a historic 1997 Nike commercial, the Chicago Bulls legend chose to talk about his mistakes instead of his titles.
articles.body:
MIn a historic Nike commercial from 1997, the Chicago Bulls legend chose to talk about his mistakes instead of his titles. A year later, he would close out his time in Chicago with the shot that gave him his sixth championship.

Michael Jordan had already won five NBA rings when he decided to talk about his defeats . In 1997, the Chicago Bulls legend starred in Nike’s “Failure” commercial, in which he revisited some of the mistakes that marked his career before becoming one of the most successful players in history.

Jordan also had to wait to win his first title

The Bulls' path to the championships was not immediate either. Chicago fell to the Detroit Pistons in the playoffs for three consecutive seasons, between 1988 and 1990. In 1991, Jordan and the Bulls finally overcame that barrier and won their first NBA championship.

By the time he starred in the commercial, Jordan had already won five titles and five regular-season MVP awards . Nike’s campaign, however, chose to show the other side of his career: the shots that didn’t go in, the games he lost, and the times when he couldn’t decide a game in his team’s favor.

One year later came the shot that ended his time in Chicago

The phrase “Failure” took on a special meaning one year later. In the 1998 Finals, the Bulls once again faced the Utah Jazz, the same opponent they had defeated in the 1997 championship series.

On June 14, 1998, in Game 6 of the Finals, Chicago was trailing 86-85 when Jordan recovered the ball after stealing it from Karl Malone. On the next possession, he got past Bryon Russell and made a mid-range shot with 5.2 seconds remaining to put the Bulls ahead 87-86. Utah did not score again, and Chicago won its sixth championship.

articles.standfirst: The NBA legend let loose on the golf course, and fans couldn't help but join the vibe
articles.summary: The NBA legend let loose on the golf course, and fans couldn't help but join the vibe
articles.body:
LeBron James has no problem enjoying life, and he makes sure the world knows it . In a world where his name is constantly making headlines across sports and his decisions are always under scrutiny, t he NBA legend still finds time to enjoy a regular Sunday without letting anything get in his way.

James literally danced to the rhythm of how little things seem to bother him . The NBA legend spent his Sunday playing golf, and it was probably a great round because his mood was hard to beat. Perhaps all the practice he has put in is paying off, allowing him t o enjoy the sport as a hobby rather than a competition.

LeBron James turns a golf club into a dance prop

James showed off his forbidden moves with a golf club, clearly enjoying his day. Fans couldn't help but catch the vibe and started wondering what had put him in such a good mood. Some of the theories were simple: he just genuinely enjoys playing golf.

The way he was moving with the club made it look as though he had just hit a great shot. He shared the moment on his Instagram Stories, revealing that he had gone to the driving range to hit a few balls before heading out for a quick nine holes. James described the late-afternoon outing as a form of therapy and celebrated golf as a beautiful game. His dance steps were funny, but that only made it easier for fans to go along with him.

A new deal could be another reason to celebrate

Others suggested his mood might have something to do with his new endorsement deal with Polymarket, which is reportedly set to reward him handsomely after he took a pay cut. James previously promoted sports betting company DraftKings Inc. an d is now part of Team Polymarket, the prediction market company.

According to Front Office Sports, J ames is not an investor in the company and will serve only as an endorser. His content and social media posts will focus on football and non-basketball topics to stay within the NBA's rules on prediction markets and betting. The deal is reportedly worth $15 million , although its length has not been determined. Investments outside basketball, including stakes in professional sports teams, have helped James build a billionaire fortune. While James no longer needs a massive NBA salary, the Polymarket deal will help offset his sharply lower earnings on the court this season.

articles.title: The NBA should be worried: The Spurs’ young core is years away from its prime
articles.standfirst: Everything begins with Wembanyama, who has established himself as one of the league's most dominant two-way players
articles.summary: Everything begins with Wembanyama, who has established himself as one of the league's most dominant two-way players
articles.body:
T he San Antonio Spurs entered last season hoping to take another step forward. Instead, they accelerated their timeline in dramatic fashion. A team that won 34 games in 2024-25 exploded for 62 victories, reached the NBA Finals and established itself as one of the league’s premier young contenders.

While the Spurs ultimately fell short of a championship, the bigger picture should leave the organization feeling optimistic heading into the 2026-27 campaign. The reason is remarkably simple: their most important players are still incredibly young.

Victor Wembanyama is just 22 years old. Stephon Castle is 21. Dylan Harper is 20. Most franchises would be thrilled to have one cornerstone player at that age. The Spurs have three. That reality changes the way San Antonio should view both its present and its future.

It all starts with Victor Wembanyama

Everything begins with Wembanyama , who has already established himself as one of the NBA’s most dominant two-way players. The 7-foot-3 star averaged 24.3 points, 11.0 rebounds and a league-leading 3.8 blocks during the 2024-25 season before the franchise built a Finals contender around him. His combination of rim protection, shooting ability and playmaking remains unlike anything the league has seen in years.

The remarkable part is that Wembanyama is still years away from the age when most superstars reach their peak. History suggests elite big men often enter their best seasons in their mid-to-late twenties. If that pattern holds true, the Spurs may not have seen the best version of Wembanyama yet.

Castle and Harper only strengthen that outlook. Castle , the 2024-25 Rookie of the Year, quickly developed into the ideal backcourt complement for Wembanyama . His versatility, defense and ability to impact games in multiple ways helped transform San Antonio from an intriguing young team into a legitimate contender. The former UConn star already looks comfortable in high-pressure situations despite being just 21 years old.

Then there is Harper, whose rookie season provided a glimpse of what the Spurs could become over the next several years. During the Western Conference Finals, Harper delivered performances that belied his age. In one memorable victory against Oklahoma City , the 20-year-old posted 24 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and seven steals while stepping into a larger role. His playoff poise reinforced why San Antonio viewed him as too talented to pass up with the No. 2 overall pick.

The Spurs are no longer the league's up-and-coming surprise. After winning 62 games and reaching the NBA Finals , they will enter the season with a target on their backs. Every opponent will treat a matchup against San Antonio as a measuring-stick game, and the margin for error will be much smaller than it was a year ago.

There are also basketball questions that still need answers. Dylan Harper is immensely talented, but integrating a 20-year-old guard into a roster with championship aspirations is rarely a seamless process. The Spurs must continue balancing his development with the urgency of competing for a title.

The backcourt rotation remains another storyline to watch. De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Harper all deserve significant on-ball opportunities, and managing those responsibilities will be one of the biggest challenges facing head coach Mitch Johnson. Finding the right balance could determine whether San Antonio's offense reaches another level.

Health will be equally important. Wembanyama has already experienced injury and health setbacks early in his career, making his availability one of the franchise's most important variables. The Spurs have improved their depth, but no contender can fully replace a player of his caliber. And while youth is a tremendous advantage, it can also create growing pains. Championship teams often learn difficult lessons before breaking through.

articles.body:
After one of the most turbulent summers of his NBA career and eventually signing with the Philadelphia 76ers , LeBron James is enjoying a well-deserved break before returning to action with his new team.

The NBA superstar returned to a familiar setting on Monday, attending SoFi Stadium to watch Monday Night Football between the Los Angeles Rams and the New York Giants .

The Rams entered the matchup looking to bounce back after a disappointing 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in their Week 1 game in Melbourne .

LeBron James’ viral reaction during MNF

James watched the game from a luxury suite at SoFi Stadium , a venue he has visited several times to support the Rams. Although he no longer wears the colors of the Los Angeles Lakers , the four-time NBA MVP remains closely connected to the NFL franchise .

The 42-year-old superstar was impressed by Los Angeles’ explosive start on offense, especially Matthew Stafford ’s touchdown pass in the first quarter, a play that electrified SoFi Stadium and gave the Rams early control of the game.

LeBron’s presence did not go unnoticed either, as social media erupted with reactions from fans excited to see the NBA legend enjoying the game.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard won a championship the last time he played for Toronto. Can he do it again?
articles.standfirst: The player who led Toronto to its first NBA title returns to the franchise after a season in which he posted the highest scoring average of his career.
articles.summary: The player who led Toronto to its first NBA title returns to the franchise after a season in which he posted the highest scoring average of his career.
articles.body:
Some returns simply grab attention, while others come with a story that still carries weight. Kawhi Leonard is back with the Toronto Raptors , and that inevitably brings back memories of the season that ended in the only way the franchise could have hoped for: with a championship.

The last time ended with the trophy in his hands

Leonard joined Toronto for the 2018-19 season after being traded from San Antonio . What followed became one of the most important chapters in Raptors history.

In his only season with the franchise, Kawhi helped Toronto win the first NBA championship in team history. The series against Golden State ended 4-2, and Leonard was named Finals MVP .

After winning the title, he took a different path. He became a free agent and signed with the Los Angeles Clippers , leaving behind a season that would forever be associated with the Toronto jersey.

Now that jersey is part of his present again.

Toronto is no longer that team

The reunion is not happening with the same roster that won the championship. The Raptors have built a different project and enter the 2026-27 season after finishing the previous campaign with a 46-36 record , good for fifth place in the Eastern Conference.

Their playoff run ended in the first round against Cleveland, with the series finishing 3-4. Still, Toronto had taken a significant step forward compared with the previous season, winning 16 more games during the regular season.

That growth is what makes Leonard's return so interesting. He is not joining a team that is simply trying to find an identity , but a roster that had already begun showing signs of progress and now adds a player with experience on the biggest stage.

Kawhi is coming off his highest-scoring season

This is where one of the most intriguing details of this second chapter comes in.

During the 2025-26 season, while playing for the Clippers , Leonard averaged 27.9 points per game across 65 appearances. It was the highest scoring average of his career.

The number is especially notable because it came in his 14th season as a professional.

His return already comes with a contract

The new chapter also came with a significant commitment from the franchise.

Leonard agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, which includes a player option for the 2028-29 season . The deal came after the NBA concluded its investigation into Leonard and the Clippers over potential salary-cap irregularities.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg set to terrorize the entire NBA in 2026-27 according to insider workouts
articles.standfirst: The Rookie of the Year is preparing for his next evolution, and offseason workouts suggest Cooper Flagg could become one of the league’s biggest problems.
articles.summary: The Rookie of the Year is preparing for his next evolution, and offseason workouts suggest Cooper Flagg could become one of the league’s biggest problems.
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks are less than a month away from tipping off their 2026-27 NBA season, a campaign generating massive expectations around Cooper Flagg . The reigning Rookie of the Year is looking to take the next leap in his development as a franchise cornerstone after being selected first overall in the 2025 Draft.

Flagg’s continued growth remains one of the most closely watched storylines in Dallas . NBA personal trainer Matt MacKenzie recently addressed the young star’s size and the impact it could have on his development.

“I haven’t put a measuring tape next to him, so I can’t confirm or deny if he’s grown in height. All I can say is he’s had one hell of an offseason. And no matter if he’s 6-9, 6-10 or 6-11, he’s going to be a problem,” MacKenzie said, according to NBA insider Marc Stein on X (formerly Twitter).

Flagg’s combination of size, athleticism, and rare mobility for a player of his height was a major reason he emerged as one of the most highly touted prospects in recent years . If he truly added inches over the summer, his physical presence could make him even more disruptive at the NBA level.

The next major step in his evolution will be developing a more consistent outside shot—one of the few areas where he struggled as a rookie. If he becomes a reliable three-point threat, defenses will have to respect him farther from the basket. That spacing would open driving lanes to the paint and enhance his effectiveness as an off-ball player, a key skill as he shares the court with Kyrie Irving .

The Mavericks officially open the new season on October 21 against the Houston Rockets , launching a campaign in which Flagg will aim to prove he is ready to become one of the league’s new faces.

articles.title: LeBron James looks erratic in misleading compilation, but the full footage tells another story
articles.standfirst: A viral edit collected only the NBA legend’s worst misses
articles.summary: A viral edit collected only the NBA legend’s worst misses
articles.body:
LeBron James appeared unable to buy a basket. A viral compilation showed the NBA’s all-time leading scorer missing three-pointers, hitting the side of the backboard and repeatedly watching the ball bounce violently off the rim during an offseason open run.

The footage was real, but the story it presented was incomplete. The minute-long video gathered James’ worst attempts from a session lasting approximately one hour, creating the impression that the 41-year-old struggled throughout the entire run.

The complete LeBron James video changes the story

The open run took place at Crespi Carmelite High School in Los Angeles and included several NBA players . James shared the court with DeMar DeRozan, Jaren Jackson Jr., Jalen Johnson, DeAndre Jordan, Peyton Watson, Isaiah Collier and Noah Clowney, among others.

James certainly missed some ugly shots, and the viral compilation did not need to manufacture those moments. Its misleading effect came from removing nearly everything he did well and presenting a collection of mistakes as if it represented his entire performance.

The complete footage showed the less dramatic reality: James experienced good and bad stretches but still converted more than half of his shots against NBA-level competition.

LeBron will return to an NBA court for a record-extending 24th season , beginning a new chapter with the Philadelphia 76ers after signing a two-year, $8 million contract that includes a player option for the second season.

Already the league’s all-time leading scorer, James will join Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown as he continues adding to his historic résumé and pursues a fifth championship in what he has described as the final chapter of his career.

articles.title: Meet the Rule-Bending Trio Set to Explode in LA: Inside the Lakers’ Unconventional Big 3
articles.standfirst: Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler make up the Lakers' Big 3 in the post-LeBron era
articles.summary: Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler make up the Lakers' Big 3 in the post-LeBron era
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers of year 0 post LeBron James will need their new "Big 3" , led by Luka Doncic , to look dominant in order to win their 18th championship ring after four seasons without making the playoffs .

Doncic has already proven that he is a great NBA star, Austin Reaves must reach the All-Star level and the giant Walker Kessler (2.18 m) has to transform into an elite defensive center.

Who is the enigmatic Walker Kessler, the 7-foot-2 center who can change Lakers history?

Kessler (25 years old) comes from playing only five games last season after suffering a tear in his left shoulder that required surgery and ended his campaign.

At the core of every great Lakers team is a dominant big man. Walker Kessler has established himself as one of the elite centers capable of performing at a very high level on both offense and defense

To complete this particular "Big 3," the Lakers mortgaged their future for Kessler, giving up two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz, which means they will not have any tradable first-round picks for the next seven years.

"At the core of every great Lakers team is a dominant big man. Walker Kessler has established himself as one of the elite centers capable of performing at a very high level on both offense and defense. articles.standfirst: Kwame Brown claims that LeBron James is "a marketing machine" that "has ruined careers"
articles.summary: Kwame Brown claims that LeBron James is "a marketing machine" that "has ruined careers"
articles.body:
K wame Brown , the number 1 pick in the 2001 Draft who fell from grace, did not mince words when speaking about LeBron James 's impact in an NBA locker room.'

"I thought LeBron was just another individual, but then I realized he is part of a group. LeBron is a machine. He is a marketing machine. He is not an individual," explained the 44-year-old former player in statements made on " The Basketball Show" .

LeBron James is a marketing machine. He is not an individual

'Kwame Brown: "If you look at the careers LeBron James has ruined..."'

'Kwame Brown, who played for the Lakers from 2005 to 2008 but never played alongside "King" James , shared that "when I realized that... when you're dealing with a machine, it generates toxic waste. What is designed to look good ends up destroying what surrounds it".'

"And if you look at the careers he has ruined: Westbrook... You have Dalton Knecht; because of LeBron's son (Bronny James), he didn't have the chance to develop... And he gets there with Andrew Wiggins, who was the first overall draft pick. I know what that's like," he accused.

articles.title: Zion Williamson denies the rape allegations and maintains that he had a consensual relationship
articles.standfirst: In his legal response, the Pelicans player denies all the allegations, maintains that the relationship ended in May 2023, and argues that the reported offenses are time-barred and that California laws do not apply to the alleged acts.
articles.summary: In his legal response, the Pelicans player denies all the allegations, maintains that the relationship ended in May 2023, and argues that the reported offenses are time-barred and that California laws do not apply to the alleged acts.
articles.body:
Zion Williamson filed his response to a lawsuit by a woman who accuses him of rape and of assaults over several years. In court documents reviewed, the New Orleans Pelicans forward issued a general denial of all the allegations in the complaint, filed under the name Jane Doe, and maintains that she did not suffer any harm because of him.

Williamson describes the relationship as a “friends with benefits” friendship and maintains that the interactions between them were cordial and consensual. According to his response, there were never any assaults or sexual violence. The player asks that the lawsuit be dismissed in its entirety.

An "informal" relationship, according to his defense

According to the document, Williamson and the plaintiff never lived together. His defense describes the sexual relationship between them as friendly and casual and claims that she repeatedly tried to initiate encounters while he was often busy or out of town.

The filing places the end of the relationship in May 2023. From that date onward, Williamson argues that the claims of assault, sexual assault, domestic violence, and harassment are time-barred under the statutes of limitations that, according to his defense, apply.

Regarding the domestic violence charge, his defense considers it "nonsensical". The reasoning is that they did not share a residence nor see each other with the frequency necessary for the relationship to be treated as domestic.

When the lawsuit became known, Williamson's lawyer said the allegations were “categorically false and irresponsible” and that they were unequivocally denied. He also stated that Williamson and the plaintiff had not been in a romantic relationship, but rather a “consensual and casual” relationship that had ended years earlier.

In addition, the defense maintained that the plaintiff began demanding millions of dollars from him after the relationship ended and claimed that Williamson had reported to the authorities what he considered attempts at extortion .

In the response presented now, a more detailed version from Williamson does appear, although again within a court document and not in an interview or personal statement.

The defense questions the application of California law

The response adds a territorial argument. Williamson maintains that California laws on sexual assault, domestic violence, and harassment do not apply to the alleged interactions, which according to the filing took place in North Carolina, Texas, and Louisiana . In addition, he denies that this type of conduct occurred in those states, in California, or anywhere else.

The lawsuit was filed in May 2025. The woman then accused Williamson of raping her, assaulting her, and terrorizing her during the years their relationship lasted. Williamson denied the accusations from the outset, and his defense also maintained that the plaintiff was trying to obtain money through extortion threats.

The filing constitutes Williamson's response to the lawsuit and not a court ruling. The plaintiff's allegations and the player's denials are the parties' positions, which must be evaluated during the proceedings . Williamson asks that the case be dismissed, a request that the court must now decide.

articles.title: Kevin Durant defends ‘flourishing’ WNBA, dismisses trans eligibility drama as outside noise
articles.standfirst: Rockets star backs the WNBA's progress while dismissing the surrounding political debate
articles.summary: Rockets star backs the WNBA's progress while dismissing the surrounding political debate
articles.body:
Kevin Durant has made it clear he won't let the ongoing WNBA controversy distract him from what he sees as the league's remarkable progress.

The Houston Rockets star addressed the debate surrounding transgender eligibility in women's basketball at media day, with former Oklahoma City Thunder teammate Enes Kanter Freedom at the center of the dispute.

Durant was asked about the growing arguments surrounding the WNBA and responded bluntly. He described the controversy as “noise” and insisted the league is “flourishing,” making it clear that his attention remains on the development of women's basketball rather than the political debate surrounding it.

“So a lot of that stuff, the politics that they bring into sports nowadays, I understand the message in behind what they're trying to do, but a person like me who just strictly cares for the purity of the sport, I do not give a f*** about none of that.,” said Durant .

His comments come after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham reignited discussion in July when she spoke about protecting young girls from competing against biological males.

Kanter Freedom subsequently declared himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft and later became involved in a heated incident at a Chicago Sky game. He was ejected from the arena and has since sued the Sky, alleging that his rights were violated.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement states that only women are eligible to play, although the agreement doesn't provide a specific definition of “woman.” Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is also preparing to retire at the end of 2026, following a period of substantial expansion and commercial growth for the league.

Durant wants basketball to remain the focus

Durant pointed toward the WNBA's expanding audience, rising player earnings and growing commercial influence. He highlighted the league's prominent stars, their endorsement deals and the businesses they've developed away from the court.

The league's momentum is also reflected in its new seven-year collective bargaining agreement, which includes significant increases in salaries and player benefits.

The WNBA has announced plans to expand to 18 teams by 2030, while the league has continued to report strong attendance, viewership and merchandise figures.

Kanter Freedom responded directly to Durant on social media, arguing that the Rockets star was dismissing an issue he considers far more serious. The former NBA player said he was standing up for women and future generations and questioned why Durant viewed the subject through a political lens.

“This isn’t about politics,” wrote Kanter Freedom. “It’s about common sense, morality, and standing up for what’s right. But what would you expect from someone who turned his back on Oklahoma to chase a ring?”

Durant's attention, however, soon returned to his preparations for another NBA season. The 37-year-old also pushed back against plans to reduce his workload because of his age, arguing that he remains most effective when he's on the court.

Houston head coach Ime Udoka and the Rockets' front office have reason to manage Durant carefully, particularly with the veteran entering another season deep into his career. The team wants to keep him healthy for the long term while maintaining enough depth to compete throughout the season.

articles.title: Delonte West reappears with a new smile: the change that comes after 10 months sober
articles.standfirst: The former NBA player appeared in public again with a completely renewed set of teeth and a much healthier appearance. The change comes after several months in which he has documented progress in his recovery and sobriety.
articles.summary: The former NBA player appeared in public again with a completely renewed set of teeth and a much healthier appearance. The change comes after several months in which he has documented progress in his recovery and sobriety.
articles.body:
Delonte West is drawing attention again, but this time because of a very different image from the ones that worried NBA fans for years. The former point guard, 42, recently appeared in a video showing off his new smile after undergoing dental reconstruction treatment. The images quickly went viral on social media and sparked a wave of supportive messages.

The physical transformation coincides with another fact that explains why his reappearance has generated such an impact: West has been drug-free for around 10 months, according to the reports that accompanied his latest public appearances. In March, he had announced that he had reached 100 days of sobriety, so this new milestone represents another step in the process.

A dental reconstruction in the midst of his recovery

The new set of teeth is part of a restoration process aimed at addressing the deterioration of the former point guard's oral health. The most recent reports indicate that West received dental implants and that the change was visible during a recent broadcast.

For years, the former basketball player went through problems related to addiction , his mental health, financial difficulties, and periods in which he ended up living on the streets.

His diagnosis of bipolar disorder became public in 2008. The combination of those problems also ended up affecting his physical appearance and his life away from the courts.

Now, the story is told from another place. Recent images show a smiling, active West with a much healthier appearance.

The support network that never disappeared

West has also had the support of people linked to the NBA for years . Mark Cuban, then owner of the Dallas Mavericks, personally intervened in 2020 to help him enter a rehabilitation center. The help did not definitively resolve his problems, but it was part of the various attempts to support him during his most difficult moments.

LeBron James, West's teammate during their time in Cleveland, has also kept in touch with people close to the former player and has shown concern for his situation over the years. At the same time, the NBA 2K universe once again opened a professional door for him: West will return to the franchise in NBA 2K27 and, according to reports, will receive payments for the use of his name and image starting in March 2027.

Fans’ reaction to his new images has been mostly positive. Many celebrated seeing him in better shape after years of worrying news and remembered the player who went on to play nine seasons in the NBA, with stints in Boston, Seattle, Cleveland, and Dallas.

The transformation of Delonte West not only represents a physical change, but also the reflection of a profound personal renewal that has touched the heart of the basketball community. After images of his new smile went viral, social media was flooded with a huge wave of empathy, faith, and hope.

Among the thousands of messages of support, fans expressed their excitement with words such as "I'm glad to see West is doing well" and "I'm glad to see you're doing better." For many, this achievement is a reminder that redemption is always possible, as one follower summed it up in a heartfelt message of encouragement: "All glory be to God. Keep going, Delonte. Many are rooting for you. With God, all things are possible. Good luck!" These comments show that, beyond the courts, the public continues to cheer West on in the most important game of all: rebuilding his own life.

The new smile is only the visible part of a much broader process: West is trying to regain stability while moving forward, day by day, in his recovery.

articles.title: Stephen Curry declares ‘no drama’ over pending contract extension to keep Warriors vibe intact
articles.standfirst: Warriors superstar remains patient on extension talks while keeping his focus firmly on winning
articles.summary: Warriors superstar remains patient on extension talks while keeping his focus firmly on winning
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has made it clear that his unresolved contract situation won’t become a distraction for the Golden State Warriors as they prepare for another NBA season.

With training camp approaching, the franchise superstar remains eligible for a new extension, but he doesn’t appear to be in a hurry to finalize an agreement.

Curry’s message is simple as he thinks the focus should remain on basketball, not contract negotiations.

“I don’t want there to be no drama,” Curry told ESPN. “No talking points. This team should be competitive and go win.”

The contract situation is significant because Curry is eligible for a two-year extension worth as much as $136.7 million. Golden State has reportedly discussed several possibilities with its longtime star, including the maximum salary, a smaller deal that could provide the organization with additional financial flexibility, or waiting before reaching a decision.

Curry appears willing to take his time and consider the bigger picture. His next contract could have implications not only for his future but also for the Warriors’ ability to strengthen the roster around him.

“It's going to happen at the right time, once I have all the information I need to make the decision that is right,” Curry said.

“The team's been great having that conversation back and forth. If I don't sign, it won't affect me in terms of my play or carrying that weight. But I'll make the decision when I'm ready.”

Curry is balancing his future with Golden State’s flexibility

Golden State’s salary-cap situation could shift considerably depending on the size and length of Curry’s next deal. A maximum extension would give Curry significant financial security, while accepting less could leave the Warriors with more room to make moves around their veteran centerpiece.

That flexibility matters to Curry because he remains focused on competing. He has repeatedly indicated that his goal is to stay with Golden State for the remainder of his career, but he also wants the roster to have the resources needed to contend.

That mindset comes as Curry prepares for his 18th NBA season. The 38-year-old was limited to 43 games last season because of persistent right-knee pain and swelling. However, he has indicated that he feels ready physically and is looking forward to getting back on the court.

“I feel like there’s no hesitation about where I’m at physically going in,” Curry said.

The Warriors will therefore enter training camp with their biggest contract question still unanswered. However, Curry’s approach suggests the situation won’t dominate the team’s preparations.

With the veteran guard committed to maintaining his focus and the organization continuing discussions, there’s no immediate need for either side to force a resolution.

The contract situation is significant because Curry is eligible for a two-year extension worth as much as $136.7 million. Golden State has reportedly discussed several possibilities with its longtime star, including the maximum salary, a smaller deal that could provide the organization with additional financial flexibility, or waiting before reaching a decision.

Curry appears willing to take his time and consider the bigger picture. His next contract could have implications not only for his future but also for the Warriors’ ability to strengthen the roster around him.
“It's going to happen at the right time, once I have all the information I need to make the decision that is right,” Curry said.
“The team's been great having that conversation back and forth. If I don't sign, it won't affect me in terms of my play or carrying that weight. But I'll make the decision when I'm ready.”
Curry is balancing his future with Golden State’s flexibility

Golden State’s salary-cap situation could shift considerably depending on the size and length of Curry’s next deal. A maximum extension would give Curry significant financial security, while accepting less could leave the Warriors with more room to make moves around their veteran centerpiece.

That flexibility matters to Curry because he remains focused on competing. He has repeatedly indicated that his goal is to stay with Golden State for the remainder of his career, but he also wants the roster to have the resources needed to contend.

That mindset comes as Curry prepares for his 18th NBA season. The 38-year-old was limited to 43 games last season because of persistent right-knee pain and swelling. However, he has indicated that he feels ready physically and is looking forward to getting back on the court.
“I feel like there’s no hesitation about where I’m at physically going in,” Curry said.
The Warriors will therefore enter training camp with their biggest contract question still unanswered. However, Curry’s approach suggests the situation won’t dominate the team’s preparations.
With the veteran guard committed to maintaining his focus and the organization continuing discussions, there’s no immediate need for either side to force a resolution.

articles.title: Russell Westbrook sets his sights on Los Angeles 2028 with a mission beyond basketball
articles.standfirst: The former NBA guard is backing a clean-energy initiative that aims to tackle pollution
articles.summary: The former NBA guard is backing a clean-energy initiative that aims to tackle pollution
articles.body:
Russell Westbrook spent nearly two decades making his mark in the NBA , but his latest challenge has little to do with what happens on the basketball court. The former point guard is now working to address air pollution in Los Angeles , the city where he grew up, while helping create opportunities for young people through clean technology.

The former UCLA standout has partnered with the Los Angeles Cleantech Incubator (LACI) to support a campaign focused on reducing emissions and expanding access to green jobs . The initiative aims to help Los Angeles make progress toward cleaner air before the 2028 Summer Olympics , when the city will welcome the world's attention.

Westbrook wants to help clean up the city

For Westbrook, the project is personal. Growing up in the South Los Angeles area, he saw the communities that continue to be affected by pollution. Heavy truck traffic carrying goods from the Port of Los Angeles contributes to the problem, with exhaust passing through neighborhoods like those where he spent his childhood.

The campaign seeks funding for the electrification of municipal and commercial vehicle fleets, alongside the development of clean-energy infrastructure and workforce training programs . Its ambitions extend beyond the Olympic Games, with t he goal of creating lasting benefits for residents.

Westbrook's involvement also reflects his long-standing belief that ambitious goals should not be dismissed simply because they appear difficult to achieve.

His work with young people goes beyond the basketball court

The initiative builds on a broader commitment to education and career opportunities that Westbrook has pursued for years through his Why Not? Foundation.

Since its launch in 2012, the foundation has worked with Los Angeles organizations on projects that include providing laptops to students and supporting training in fields such as coding and engineering.

One of its major projects is Westbrook Academy, a charter middle and high school in South Los Angeles developed in partnership with the L.A. Promise Fund. The school opened a new campus in 2024, featuring modern classrooms and science laboratories, with a focus on science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Westbrook has also used sporting events to introduce young people to career paths they might not otherwise consider. During the NBA All-Star events in Los Angeles , his foundation partnered with workforce-development organizations to highlight opportunities in clean technology.

For Westbrook, sports can serve as a connection point, helping young fans discover possibilities beyond the court and the field.

Source: Mosi Secret, National Geographic.

articles.title: Did Lonzo Ball just call it a career? Former No. 2 pick explains cryptic post-tense comments
articles.standfirst: The Cavaliers free agent explains why his comments were misunderstood
articles.summary: The Cavaliers free agent explains why his comments were misunderstood
articles.body:
Lonzo Ball briefly had basketball fans wondering whether his NBA career was over, but the former No. 2 overall pick has now made it clear that retirement isn't on his mind just yet.

The 28-year-old guard sparked speculation after speaking openly about his injury-plagued career during the latest episode of the “Ball in the Family” podcast. Ball reflected on the opportunities basketball had given him and admitted that he never reached the level he believed he could have.

“To be honest, I don't think I ever got to my peak,” Ball said. “I feel like I gave everything I had to hoop and I feel like everything I got in my life is because of hoop.

“So I'm grateful to even make it to the league and even be able to play for nine years. That's how I look at it.”

Ball's comments quickly spread online, with some fans interpreting his words as a farewell. His reflections on fulfilling his childhood dream of playing in the NBA, combined with his acceptance of what his body would allow him to do, certainly sounded like a player looking back on a completed career.

However, Ball hadn't actually announced his retirement.

Lonzo says he's still waiting for an NBA opportunity

The former UCLA star put the speculation to rest Wednesday with a post on X. Responding sarcastically to reports that he had retired, Ball wrote: “I retired? News to me lol cuz I'm still waiting for a call… NBA season long ”

The message confirms that Ball remains interested in playing and is currently waiting for an NBA team to offer him an opportunity. He's an unrestricted free agent after spending the 2025-26 season with the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Ball's career has taken a difficult route since the Los Angeles Lakers selected him second overall in the 2017 NBA Draft.

After two seasons in Los Angeles, he was traded to the New Orleans Pelicans as part of the deal that sent Anthony Davis to the Lakers. He later joined the Chicago Bulls, where his career was dramatically disrupted by a serious left-knee injury.

The injury required several procedures and forced Ball to miss the entire 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons. He eventually returned to NBA action in 2024-25, completing a comeback that had once seemed uncertain.

Ball then moved to Cleveland and appeared in 35 games during the 2025-26 season. He averaged 4.6 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game while playing 20.8 minutes a night.

Despite his latest struggles, Ball's own words indicate that he hasn't closed the door on basketball. His podcast appearance was seemingly more about coming to terms with what injuries had taken from him than announcing the end of his career.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton gives his final Hali 1 a personal meaning before revealing what comes next
articles.summary: Tyrese Haliburton’s last Hali 1 colorway carries more than the Pacers’ colors. As he shows off the “Pace” in the video, he explains why this was the pair he wanted for his return.
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton’s last Hali 1 colorway carries more than the Pacers’ colors. As he shows off the “Pace” in the video, he explains why this was the pair he wanted for his return.

“I thought it was important for my comeback pair to be something that not only tied me to my team, but I think the city as well,” Haliburton says. After his Achilles injury, he wanted his return to feel connected to home in Indiana.

The shoe brings together Pacers yellow and navy blue. Haliburton thinks fans will wear it because it matches so much of the team’s gear—a detail that matters to him as much as how it looks on his own feet.

Then he drops the news sneaker fans were waiting for: “This would be my final one cause it’s time to get ready for the two.” The “Pace” closes the Hali 1 line as he begins looking ahead to the Hali 2.

PUMA lists the “Pace” for October 23 at $130
